q: What comes next in the series: 3, 2, 5, 4, 7, 8, 9, ?
x: Two interleaved series: one adds 2 each time (3, 5...), the other multiplies by 2 (2, 4...). The next term is 16.

q: What comes next in the series: 10, 1, 15, 2, 20, 4, 25, ?
x: Two interleaved series: one adds 5 each time (10, 15...), the other multiplies by 2 (1, 2...). The next term is 8.

q: What comes next in the series: 2, 5, 6, 10, 10, 20, 14, ?
x: Two interleaved series: one adds 4 each time (2, 6...), the other multiplies by 2 (5, 10...). The next term is 40.

q: What comes next in the series: 20, 1, 17, 3, 14, 9, 11, ?
x: Two interleaved series: one subtracts 3 each time (20, 17...), the other multiplies by 3 (1, 3...). The next term is 27.

q: What comes next in the series: 3, 4, 6, 10, 18, 34, ?
x: The gaps are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, doubling. The next gap is 32. 34 + 32 = 66.

q: What comes next in the series: 1, 3, 6, 11, 18, 29, ?
x: The gaps are the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. The next prime is 13. 29 + 13 = 42.

q: What comes next in the series: 0, 1, 9, 36, 100, ?
x: The gaps are 1, 8, 27, 64 (cubes), so the next is 125. 100 + 125 = 225.

q: What comes next in the series: 1, 3, 9, 11, 33, 35, 105, ?
x: The rules alternate: add 2, then multiply by 3. After x3 comes +2: 105 + 2 = 107.

q: What comes next in the series: 2, 5, 10, 13, 26, 29, 58, ?
x: The rules alternate: add 3, then multiply by 2. After x2 comes +3: 58 + 3 = 61.

q: What comes next in the series: 1, 5, 10, 14, 28, 32, 64, ?
x: The rules alternate: add 4, then multiply by 2. After x2 comes +4: 64 + 4 = 68.

q: What comes next in the series: 1, 4, 27, 16, 125, 36, ?
x: Odd positions are cubes (1, 27, 125, next 343); even positions are squares (4, 16, 36).

q: What letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ?
x: Steps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next is +6. O is 15, and 15 + 6 = 21, which is U.

q: What letter comes next: Z, X, U, Q, L, ?
x: Steps are -2, -3, -4, -5, so the next is -6. L is 12, and 12 - 6 = 6, which is F.

q: What comes next: J, F, M, A, M, J, ?
x: These are the first letters of the months: January, February, ... June, then July.

q: What comes next: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, ?
x: First letters of One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven, so next is Eight, E.

q: A price goes up 10% and then down 10%. Compared with the start, the final price is what?
x: Factor is (1+0.1) x (1-0.1) = 1 - 0.01 so it is 1% lower.

q: A price goes up 20% and then down 20%. Compared with the start, the final price is what?
x: Factor is (1+0.2) x (1-0.2) = 1 - 0.04 so it is 4% lower.

q: A price goes up 30% and then down 30%. Compared with the start, the final price is what?
x: Factor is (1+0.3) x (1-0.3) = 1 - 0.09 so it is 9% lower.

q: A coat is 20% off, then an extra 10% off the sale price. What is the total discount?
x: You pay 80% x 90% = 72% of the original, so the discount is 28%, not 30%.

q: A coat is 30% off, then an extra 20% off the sale price. What is the total discount?
x: You pay 70% x 80% = 56% of the original, so the discount is 44%, not 50%.

q: A coat is 50% off, then an extra 50% off the sale price. What is the total discount?
x: You pay 50% x 50% = 25% of the original, so the discount is 75%, not 100%.

q: A coat is 25% off, then an extra 20% off the sale price. What is the total discount?
x: You pay 75% x 80% = 60% of the original, so the discount is 40%, not 45%.

q: A number is increased by 50%, then the result is decreased by 50%. The result is 75. What was the original number?
x: 1.5 x 0.5 = 0.75 of the original, and 75 is 0.75 of 100.

q: After a 20% discount a book costs $48. What was the original price?
x: $48 is 80% of the original. 48 / 0.8 = 60.

q: A store marks up cost by 25% to get a price of $75. What was the cost?
x: Price = 1.25 x cost, so cost = 75 / 1.25 = 60.

q: A is 20% larger than B. B is what percent smaller than A?
x: A = 1.2B, so the gap 0.2B is 0.2/1.2 = 1/6, about 16.7% of A.

q: The sum of three consecutive integers is 72. What is the largest?
x: Middle = 72 / 3 = 24, so the numbers are 23, 24, 25.

q: The sum of four consecutive even numbers is 100. What is the smallest?
The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 99. What is the middle one?
x: The middle one is the mean: 99 / 3 = 33 (numbers 31, 33, 35).

q: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 156. What is their sum?
Boys and girls in a club are in the ratio 3:5 and there are 40 members. How many girls are there?
x: The ratio has 8 parts; 40 / 8 = 5 per part; girls = 5 x 5 = 25.

q: Red and blue marbles are in the ratio 2:7. There are 63 marbles. How many are red?
x: 2 + 7 = 9 parts, 63 / 9 = 7 per part, red = 2 x 7 = 14.

q: A recipe uses flour and sugar in the ratio 5:2. With 8 cups of sugar, how many cups of flour?
x: Sugar 8 is 4 times 2, so flour is 4 x 5 = 20.

q: Pump A fills a pool in 6 hours and pump B in 3 hours. Working together, how long do they take?
x: Rates: 1/6 + 1/3 = 9/18 of the pool per hour, so the time is 18/9 = 2 hours.

q: Pump A fills a pool in 12 hours and pump B in 4 hours. Working together, how long do they take?
x: Rates: 1/12 + 1/4 = 16/48 of the pool per hour, so the time is 48/16 = 3 hours.

q: Pump A fills a pool in 10 hours and pump B in 15 hours. Working together, how long do they take?
x: Rates: 1/10 + 1/15 = 25/150 of the pool per hour, so the time is 150/25 = 6 hours.

q: Two trains 300 miles apart head toward each other at 40 and 60 mph. After how many hours do they meet?
x: They close 40 + 60 = 100 miles each hour. 300 / 100 = 3 hours.

q: Two cyclists start 90 km apart and ride toward each other at 12 and 18 km/h. How many hours until they meet?
x: The gap closes at 12 + 18 = 30 km/h. 90 / 30 = 3 hours.

q: A runner at 9 mph starts 6 miles behind another at 6 mph, both going the same way. How many hours until she catches up?
x: She gains 9 - 6 = 3 mph. 6 / 3 = 2 hours.

q: A car drives to a town at 30 mph and returns the same road at 60 mph. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
x: Average speed = total distance / total time = 2ab/(a+b) = 2x30x60/90 = 40 mph, not the simple mean.

q: A car drives to a town at 40 mph and returns the same road at 60 mph. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
x: Average speed = total distance / total time = 2ab/(a+b) = 2x40x60/100 = 48 mph, not the simple mean.

q: A car drives to a town at 20 mph and returns the same road at 30 mph. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
x: Average speed = total distance / total time = 2ab/(a+b) = 2x20x30/50 = 24 mph, not the simple mean.

q: How many squares of all sizes are in a 3 by 3 grid of small squares?
x: Count by size: 9 of size 1, 4 of size 2, 1 of size 3. Total 14.

q: How many squares of all sizes are in a 5 by 5 grid of small squares?
x: Count by size: 25 of size 1, 16 of size 2, 9 of size 3, 4 of size 4, 1 of size 5. Total 55.

q: How many diagonals does a polygon with 6 sides have?
x: Each corner joins to 3 others, and each diagonal is counted twice: 6 x 3 / 2 = 9.

q: How many diagonals does a polygon with 8 sides have?
x: Each corner joins to 5 others, and each diagonal is counted twice: 8 x 5 / 2 = 20.

q: In how many different orders can 4 books be arranged on a shelf?
In how many ways can 5 people be seated in a row?
How many different ways can you choose 2 people from a group of 6?
x: Choose in order: 6 x 5 = 30, but each pair is counted twice, so 15.

q: A binary number is read right to left as 1, 2, 4, 8. What is 1011 in ordinary numbers?
What is 110 in binary, written as an ordinary number?
What is the units digit of 7 x 7 x 7 x 7?
What is the last digit of 2 to the power 10 (ten 2s multiplied)?
x: Last digits repeat 2, 4, 8, 6. Power 10 is position 2 in the cycle: 4. (2^10 = 1024)

q: What is the last digit of 3 to the power 5?
In a class of 30, 18 play soccer, 15 play chess and 5 do neither. How many play both?
x: 25 play at least one. 18 + 15 = 33, so 33 - 25 = 8 play both.

q: In a class of 40, 26 play soccer, 20 play chess and 3 do neither. How many play both?
x: 37 play at least one. 26 + 20 = 46, so 46 - 37 = 9 play both.

q: In a class of 50, 30 play soccer, 28 play chess and 8 do neither. How many play both?
x: 42 play at least one. 30 + 28 = 58, so 58 - 42 = 16 play both.

q: Starting on a Wednesday, which weekday comes 100 days later?
x: 100 = 14 weeks + 2 days. Wednesday plus 2 is Friday.

q: In 2024 (a leap year) January 1 was a Monday. What day was December 31, 2024?
x: Dec 31 is 365 days after Jan 1. 365 = 52 weeks + 1 day. Monday plus 1 is Tuesday.

q: If June 10 is a Thursday, what day is August 10 in the same year?
x: June 10 to Aug 10 is 20 + 31 + 10 = 61 days = 8 weeks + 5 days. Thursday + 5 = Tuesday.

q: Counting back 100 days from a Friday, which weekday do you reach?
x: 100 = 14 weeks + 2 days. Friday minus 2 days is Wednesday.

q: Today is Monday. What day will it be 1,000 days from now?
x: 1,000 = 142 x 7 + 6. Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.

q: How many days are there from January 1 to March 1 in a leap year, not counting the end date?
x: January 31 + February 29 = 60 days.

q: If the 3rd of a month is a Sunday, on which date is the third Friday?
x: The 3rd is Sunday, so the first Friday is the 8th. Fridays fall on the 8th, 15th and 22nd, so the third is the 22nd.

q: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands at 2:30?
x: Hour hand: 30x2 + 0.5x30 = 75 degrees. Minute hand: 6x30 = 180. The smaller gap is 105 degrees.

q: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands at 3:40?
x: Hour hand: 30x3 + 0.5x40 = 110 degrees. Minute hand: 6x40 = 240. The smaller gap is 130 degrees.

q: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands at 9:15?
x: Hour hand: 30x9 + 0.5x15 = 277.5 degrees. Minute hand: 6x15 = 90. The smaller gap is 172.5 degrees.

q: How many times do the hour and minute hands overlap in a 12-hour period (counting 12:00 once)?
x: The minute hand laps the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours.

q: A clock gains 3 minutes every hour. It is set right at noon. What time does it show at 6 PM real time?
x: 6 hours x 3 minutes = 18 extra minutes, so 6:18 PM.

q: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the chance both are red?
x: First red: 4/10. Then 3/9. Multiply: 12/90 = 2/15.

q: A bag has 5 red and 7 blue marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the chance both are red?
x: First red: 5/12. Then 4/11. Multiply: 20/132 = 5/33.

q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the chance their sum is 7?
x: Six of the 36 outcomes sum to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4 and reverses): 6/36 = 1/6.

q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the chance their sum is 10?
x: The outcomes are 4+6, 5+5, 6+4: 3 of 36 = 1/12.

q: A fair coin is flipped 3 times. What is the chance of exactly 2 heads?
x: There are 8 outcomes and 3 have exactly two heads (HHT, HTH, THH): 3/8.

q: A coin lands heads 5 times in a row. For a fair coin, what is the chance the next flip is heads?
x: Flips are independent, so each flip is 1/2 regardless of the past.

q: A box holds 3 red and 2 blue cards. One card is drawn at random. What is the chance it is blue?
x: Total 5 cards, 2 are blue: 2/5.

q: Three boxes are labeled Apples, Oranges and Mixed, all wrongly. A fruit from the Mixed box is an apple. What is in the Oranges box?
x: The Mixed label is wrong, so that box is all apples. The Oranges box cannot be oranges or apples, so it is mixed.

q: A says "B lies." B says "C lies." C says "A and B both lie." Who tells the truth?
x: If B tells the truth, C lies and A lies: consistent (C lies, A lies). Other options fail.

q: Five runners finish. Ana beat Bo, Bo beat Cy, Cy beat Dee and Eli beat Ana. Who came third?
x: The order is Eli, Ana, Bo, Cy, Dee. Third is Bo.

q: In a 4-floor building (floor 1 is the lowest), Ann lives above Bo, Cy lives below Bo and Dee lives above Ann. Who lives on floor 2?
x: From bottom to top: Cy, Bo, Ann, Dee. Floor 2 is Bo.

q: Knights always tell the truth and knaves always lie. A says "B is a knave", and B says "A and I are both knights." What are A and B?
x: If B were a knight, B's claim makes A a knight too, but A says B is a knave: contradiction. So B is a knave, and A is truthful.

q: Ann, Ben and Cal each own one pet: a cat, a dog or a fish. Ann is allergic to fur. Ben does not own a dog. Who owns the dog?
x: Ann has the fish (allergic to fur). Ben does not have the dog, so he has the cat. Cal has the dog.

q: Sue is taller than Tim. Tim is taller than Uma. Vic is shorter than Sue but taller than Tim. Who is second tallest?
x: Sue > Vic > Tim > Uma, so Vic is second.

q: Four people stand in a line. Ann is not first or last. Ben is first. Cal is not next to Ben. Cal is not last. Who is last?
x: Ben is first. Cal is not second, not last, so Cal is third. Ann is not last, so Ann is second and Dee is last.

q: There are 8 coins and one is heavier. With a balance scale, what is the fewest weighings that always find the heavy coin?
x: Weigh 3 vs 3. If they balance, the heavy coin is among 2 left. Else it is in the heavy 3. One more weighing finds it among 3. Total 2.

q: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
Lily pads double every day and cover a lake on day 48. On which day did they cover half the lake?
x: Doubling means the day before full coverage is half coverage: day 47.

q: If 3 machines make 3 widgets in 8 minutes, how many seconds do 90 machines need to make 90 widgets?
x: Each machine makes 1 widget in 8 minutes, so 90 machines make 90 in 8 minutes = 480 seconds.

q: In a race you overtake the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
x: You take the position of the runner you passed: 2nd.

q: Two fathers and two sons share 3 apples, one each, with none left over. How is that possible?
x: The grandfather and father are fathers; the father and son are sons. That is only 3 people.

q: A doctor gives you 3 pills and says to take one every half hour. How long do they last?
x: Take one now, one after 30 min, one after 60 min: 1 hour.

q: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 die. How many are left?
x: "All but 9" means 9 survive.

q: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
x: "Minute" has one M, "moment" has two, and "thousand years" has none.

q: With a 3-liter and a 5-liter jug, what is the fewest fill, pour or empty steps to measure exactly 4 liters?
x: Fill 5 (1), pour into 3 (2), empty 3 (3), pour 2 into 3 (4), fill 5 (5), pour into 3 (6): 4 left in the 5-liter jug.

q: Half of a number plus a third of it is 25. What is the number?
x: Half + third = 5/6 of the number = 25. 25 x 6/5 = 30.

q: I am thinking of a number. Double it, add 6, then halve: the result is 11. What number was it?
x: Work backward: double 11 = 22, subtract 6 = 16, halve = 8.

q: A hen and a half lays an egg and a half in a day and a half. How many eggs do 6 hens lay in 6 days?
x: Rate: 1.5 hens lay 1.5 eggs in 1.5 days, so 1 hen lays 1 egg per 1.5 days. 6 hens x 6 days / 1.5 = 24.

q: A farmer has chickens and cows with 20 heads and 56 legs. How many cows are there?
x: All chickens would be 40 legs. 16 extra legs, 2 per cow swapped: 8 cows.

q: A number is divisible by both 6 and 8. What is the smallest positive such number?
x: The least common multiple of 6 and 8 is 24.

q: How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 are divisible by both 2 and 5?
x: Divisible by 2 and 5 means by 10: 10, 20, ... 100, which is 10 numbers.
